validity_note: The scenario is reachable only with app.payments.enabled=true (application.yml defaults APP_PAYMENTS_ENABLED to false and PaymentsDisabledBootGuard then refuses to boot with paid or in-flight rows). 'More active campaigns than FREE allows' is not a concept in code: the limit is a creation quota = PartnershipOpportunity rows created inside the ACTIVE billing period, soft-deleted ones included. Live limits are FREE 5, BUSINESS 5, ENTERPRISE 10, so only ENTERPRISE or TRIAL (10) falling to FREE/BUSINESS lowers it, and every applied downgrade opens a new period at now, so the company is never 'over'. No code handles existing campaigns on downgrade or fallback.

key_facts.claim: The limit is a creation quota, not a cap on live campaigns: enforceLimit PESSIMISTIC_WRITE-locks the ACTIVE billing period, counts PartnershipOpportunity rows with createdTime BETWEEN its start and end (no active filter, no check that now lies inside the period) and throws at count >= limit; it is called only from saveFromDto (create), never from update/patch.

resolveEffectiveCampaignLimit: DOWNGRADE_PENDING, PAYMENT_FAILED and TERMS_PENDING use previousPlan.campaignLimit, SUSPENDED_LEGAL is 0, all else currentPlan. /subscription/status returns this limit, campaignsUsedThisPeriod and targetPlanName, but not the target plan's limit.
Live limits: FREE 5, BUSINESS 5, ENTERPRISE 10 (seeded 2/5/10, FREE raised to 5); a trial is the ENTERPRISE plan for 3 months.

requestDowngrade: TRIAL_ENTERPRISE to FREE is immediate with a new FREE period; otherwise only from BUSINESS_ACTIVE, ENTERPRISE_ACTIVE or PAYMENT_FAILED, it sets Stripe cancel_at_period_end (FREE) or a SubscriptionSchedule (other target), then DOWNGRADE_PENDING, previousPlan=currentPlan, targetPlan, DOWNGRADE_SCHEDULED notification. No campaign check, no check that the target is cheaper.

The FREE fallback happens only in handleSubscriptionDeleted, for both period-end cancellation after a voluntary downgrade and exhausted dunning: expire period, FREE_ACTIVE, clear subscription/schedule ids and targetPlan, new FREE period from now, event PAYMENT_EXHAUSTED, notification SUBSCRIPTION_PAYMENT_EXHAUSTED.

ENTERPRISE to BUSINESS lands via customer.subscription.updated (items/schedule changed): new plan, *_ACTIVE, new period from now, SUBSCRIPTION_DOWNGRADED. Every plan transition (checkout, updated, deleted, trial cancel/expiry) starts a period at now, so usage resets to 0; none reads or changes PartnershipOpportunity rows.

Payment failure: handlePaymentFailed has no source-state guard, sets PAYMENT_FAILED and previousPlan=currentPlan (paid limit kept), sends SUBSCRIPTION_PAYMENT_FAILED; willRetry is only logged. invoice.paid restores *_ACTIVE from previousPlan without clearing targetPlan. subscription.updated without items/schedule change (past_due, unpaid, cancel_at_period_end) is ignored.

Windows differ by plan: FREE periods roll into a new row via the cron (FREE_ACTIVE only), paid periods are extended in place by invoice.paid (endDate+1 month, startDate fixed), so paid usage accumulates until the next plan change.

Payments are off by default: SubscriptionPaidController, StripeWebhookController and TrialExpiryNotifierCronJob are bean-gated, paid cron branches and TermsGraceProcessorCronJob no-op, and the boot guard rejects in-flight paid statuses.

FE: the usage ring shows live used/limit but clamps at 100%; plan cards use hardcoded PLAN_LADDER (Free 2); downgrade CTAs exist only for ENTERPRISE_ACTIVE and BUSINESS_ACTIVE and vanish once targetPlanName is set; the dialog gets only targetPlan, currentPlanName, billingPeriodEnd and promises 'You'll keep your current benefits until then'. Nothing on the FE checks the limit before creating a campaign.

gaps.finding: No over-limit rule exists: an applied downgrade or fallback opens a fresh period, so the company keeps every live campaign and immediately gets the full lower quota; closing campaigns frees nothing (count ignores active); no BE preflight, no FE warning, no notification mentions campaigns; a limit 400 on create shows generic save_failed while the subscription.campaign_limit dialog keys are unused. REQUIREMENTS only says existing campaigns are never touched.

Quota windows are inconsistent: paid periods grow in place on invoice.paid (usage cumulative, so only a plan change such as a downgrade unblocks creation) while FREE rolls monthly; in PAYMENT_FAILED nothing extends the period and the FREE rollover skips non-FREE rows, so once endDate passes new campaigns are never counted: unlimited creation if the stale window was under limit, permanent block if not.

The downgrade-to-FREE cron is dead and the real path is mislabeled: processExpiredDowngrades matches only BillingPeriod status PENDING_DOWNGRADE, which no production code sets (tests only), though REQUIREMENTS says the cron applies it; the real switch, customer.subscription.deleted, logs PAYMENT_EXHAUSTED and sends a CRITICAL notification (email default ALWAYS) 'All payment attempts for {oldPlan} failed' to voluntary downgraders (BUSINESS targets get SUBSCRIPTION_DOWNGRADED). A missed webhook leaves DOWNGRADE_PENDING at the paid limit forever.

Limits and eligibility disagree across layers: DB FREE=5=BUSINESS (BUSINESS to FREE changes nothing), FE PLAN_LADDER Free=2 ('limits the landing tiers'), REQUIREMENTS FREE=2, an unused messages property 'Free (2 campaigns/month)'; the FE offers no downgrade in PAYMENT_FAILED although requestDowngrade allows it.

gaps.finding: Stripe-side paths break the pending state: cancelDowngrade for a BUSINESS target calls SubscriptionSchedule.cancel(), which in Stripe also cancels the attached subscription (release() keeps it), so 'Keep current plan' ends in subscription.deleted, FREE and PAYMENT_EXHAUSTED; a payment failure overwrites DOWNGRADE_PENDING and recovery restores *_ACTIVE while targetPlan and Stripe's cancel remain; a portal-side cancellation (the FE advertises plan changes there) is not mirrored until the deletion arrives as PAYMENT_EXHAUSTED.

previousPlan is overloaded: FREE fallbacks set it to the old paid plan and never clear it, yet resolveEffectiveCampaignLimit trusts it in TERMS_PENDING, so a FREE company entering TERMS_PENDING would get the old paid limit (latent: enterTermsPending has no production caller, only the e2e/dev TestSubscriptionController).

invariants: Plan changes never auto-deactivate or edit campaigns with active applications (ACCEPTED_BY_COMPANY, ACCEPTED_BY_INFLUENCER, CONTENT_APPROVED/POSTED/REJECTED): deactivateOpportunity and company update/patch refuse them, and influencers only see active=true campaigns.
DOWNGRADE_PENDING and PAYMENT_FAILED keep the previous paid entitlement until Stripe confirms the end; the local paid plan never changes before the webhook; SUSPENDED_LEGAL stays at 0.

The creation check stays atomic (count and insert in one transaction under the PESSIMISTIC_WRITE lock on the active billing period), and webhook idempotency (unique stripe_event_id, row lock on company_subscription) plus single-transaction plan+period changes are kept.
subscription_plan.campaign_limit stays the single source of limit values; FE cards, dialogs and notification copy render API values, not constants.

Payments-off deploys keep working: FREE rollover runs regardless of the toggle, paid endpoints and webhooks stay unregistered, and any new transitional status joins PaymentsDisabledBootGuard's in-flight set.
good_designs: Grandfather plus quota: keep a per-period creation quota and never touch existing campaigns, but let one entitlement policy own the window (paid periods roll monthly like FREE, a plan change does not reset usage mid-cycle, stale ACTIVE periods roll for every status) and return usage plus the target plan's limit from /subscription/status so the downgrade dialog and plan cards warn before confirming.

Explicit over-limit mode: count live campaigns (active, not ended) against the plan and, when an applied downgrade or exhausted dunning leaves the count above it, block create and reactivation (update/patch active=true) without auto-closing anything, with an FE banner and a notification that state the new cap.

Either way: handleSubscriptionDeleted branches on DOWNGRADE_PENDING/targetPlan (SUBSCRIPTION_DOWNGRADED vs PAYMENT_EXHAUSTED), the dead PENDING_DOWNGRADE path becomes a reconciliation job or is deleted, cancelDowngrade releases the schedule, webhook handlers guard source states, and the FE reads limits and eligibility from the BE.
red_flags: 'The limit caps concurrently active campaigns, so a downgraded company is blocked until it archives some': the count is campaigns created in the active period (soft-deleted included) and the downgrade opens a fresh period, so creation is allowed at once and archiving frees nothing.

'processExpiredDowngrades moves DOWNGRADE_PENDING companies to FREE at period end': it matches only BillingPeriod status PENDING_DOWNGRADE, which production code never sets; Stripe's customer.subscription.deleted does the switch.
'A failed payment drops the company to FREE limits': PAYMENT_FAILED keeps previousPlan's plan and limit; FREE comes only with customer.subscription.deleted.
'BUSINESS to FREE lowers the limit from 5 to 2': the DB has FREE=5=BUSINESS; 2 survives only in FE PLAN_LADDER, REQUIREMENTS.md and an unused messages property.

'TrialExpiryNotifierCronJob or TermsGraceProcessorCronJob enforce limits or apply downgrades': the notifier only sends 14/7/1-day trial reminders, TermsGrace suspends expired TERMS_PENDING and rewrites previous_state, and both do nothing with payments disabled.
